item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Strong -1, almost entirely for the poor usage of redaction/expungement/blackbox.

464-1 can be literally anything because zero information is given about it, which makes the Foundation destroying it instead of containing it very strange. The #14 expunged bothers me for the same reason - not enough provided to infer literally anything about why they're expunging it.

These notably included identification for the local [DATA EXPUNGED] as well as stocks of █████, rifles, and ████████.

THIS expunge is great, but the blackboxes are pointless and there's not nearly enough information to infer what they MIGHT be. Blackbox the rifles, or uncover them all.

Document 464-1 might as well not exist for all that it adds to the article. Expungement can be literally anything. I do realize I have a bit of a personal beef with expungements, but that doesn't really make these ones any better as a writing tool.

The concept is pretty solid, but there's nothing to really recommend it in this piece. Reference the Foundation using it, reference another GoI as a source for its existence, reference any reason at all for its existence - or at least improve the redactions so that we get to focus on filling in those blanks ourselves.

item.content:encoded:
This SCP makes me wonder about the Russian Army during WWII, within the Foundation universe; specifically because of their immense numbers. Given that military equipment was found within the factory, this just convinces me more that this was how they managed to produce such sturdy and willing men to die for their country in such vast quantities, although the only hole in my theory is the fact that the fourteen panels inside the observation room are written in French.

It could be theorized that since the machines are capable of producing humans of different races, that it was either altered after WWII by the Russian government (if it does, in fact, lay within Russia or any of their previous satellite countries) for the ability to create spies or sleeper agents.

I love my mind and its burst of creativity past midnight…
